Simulate cross-omic network data with known structure

Source: R/network-simulate.R
simulate_crossomic_network.Rd

Generates donor-level metabolite data and cell-type-specific transcript pseudobulk counts whose latent log-expression follows a known Gaussian graphical model, with cell-type heterogeneity and optional exposure-dependent composition. Intended for benchmarking edge recovery and false-positive control.

Usage

simulate_crossomic_network(
  n_donors = 100L,
  n_celltypes = 4L,
  n_transcripts = 30L,
  n_metabolites = 10L,
  n_cells_per_donor = 200L,
  edge_density = 0.1,
  shared_edge_frac = 0.6,
  cross_omic_frac = 0.2,
  exposure_effect = 0.5,
  composition_confounding = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n_donors

Integer; number of donors. Default 100.

n_celltypes

Integer; number of cell types. Default 4.

n_transcripts

Integer; number of transcript features. Default 30.

n_metabolites

Integer; number of metabolite features. Default 10.

n_cells_per_donor

Integer; cells per donor, allocated to cell types by the composition. Pseudobulk depth scales with the number of cells. Default 200.

edge_density

Numeric; proportion of possible edges present in the base network. Default 0.1.

shared_edge_frac

Numeric; fraction of base-network edges kept by cell types 1 and 2, each of which also gains the same number of new edges. Default 0.6.

cross_omic_frac

Numeric; fraction of edges that are cross-omic. Default 0.2.

exposure_effect

Numeric; effect of the exposure on the mean of affected features and on composition. Default 0.5.

composition_confounding

Logical; make the proportions of cell types 1 and 2 depend on the exposure. Default TRUE.

seed

Integer or NULL; random seed. The caller's random number generator state is restored on return. Default NULL.

Value

List with:

pseudobulk

List of count matrices (donors x transcripts), one per cell type.

metabolites

Metabolite matrix (donors x metabolites), shared by all cell types.

exposure

Named numeric vector of exposure values.

composition

Donor-by-cell-type matrix of proportions.

n_cells

Donor-by-cell-type matrix of simulated cell numbers.

true_networks

List of precision matrices, one per cell type, of the latent transcript log-expression and the metabolites conditional on the exposure.

true_adjacency

List of the corresponding adjacency matrices.

celltype_names

Character vector of cell type names.

node_info

DataFrame of feature metadata.

params

List of simulation parameters.

Details

Simulation design:

  1. A sparse positive-definite base precision matrix \(\Theta\) is generated over transcripts and metabolites with within-omic and cross-omic edges.

  2. Cell types 1 and 2 keep a fraction shared_edge_frac of the base edges and gain as many new edges; cell type 3 has an independently generated precision matrix; cell types 4 and above have no transcript-transcript or cross-omic edges.

  3. Metabolites are drawn once per donor from a multivariate normal distribution whose precision is the metabolite block of the base matrix, \(P_m\).

  4. For each cell type, latent transcript log-expression is drawn from its conditional distribution given the metabolites, \(N(-\Theta_{tt}^{-1}\Theta_{tm} m, \Theta_{tt}^{-1})\). The joint precision of transcripts and metabolites is then \(\Theta_{tt}\), \(\Theta_{tm}\) and \(P_m + \Theta_{mt}\Theta_{tt}^{-1}\Theta_{tm}\); it is returned in true_networks, so its metabolite block can contain edges induced by the cross-omic edges.

  5. The exposure shifts the mean of the first 30% of metabolites and, in cell types 1 and 2, of the first 20% of transcripts; it does not change any network.

  6. Pseudobulk counts are Poisson with mean equal to the number of cells times \(\exp(\text{latent} + 1)\), which makes them overdispersed relative to a Poisson with a fixed mean.

  7. If composition_confounding = TRUE, the proportions of cell types 1 and 2 increase with the exposure, so pseudobulk depth varies with the exposure.

Examples

sim <- simulate_crossomic_network(
    n_donors = 50, n_transcripts = 20,
    n_metabolites = 5, seed = 42)
names(sim)
#>  [1] "pseudobulk"     "metabolites"    "exposure"       "composition"   
#>  [5] "n_cells"        "true_networks"  "true_adjacency" "celltype_names"
#>  [9] "node_info"      "params"        
sim$true_adjacency[[1]][1:5, 1:5]
#>        gene_1 gene_2 gene_3 gene_4 gene_5
#> gene_1      0      0      0      0      0
#> gene_2      0      0      0      0      0
#> gene_3      0      0      0      0      0
#> gene_4      0      0      0      0      0
#> gene_5      0      0      0      0      0
